q: The voltage across a component is $9.0\,\text{V}$, and a current of $0.060\,\text{A}$ flows through it. What is the resistance of the component?
The length of a copper wire is halved and its cross-sectional area is doubled. How does the resistance of the wire change?
a: The resistance falls to a quarter, because $R = \rho l : A$: half the length halves the resistance and double the cross-sectional area halves it again.
